The wind rustled through the trees, a whispering breath that carried the scent of damp earth and pine needles. Ava stood at the edge of the clearing, her heart pounding in her chest like a drumbeat, echoing the rhythm of the distant waterfall that cascaded down the rocky slope. Sunlight flickered through the leaves, casting playful shadows across her face, each patch of light feeling like a gentle touch, urging her forward.

“Are you coming or just going to stare at the trees?” Liam called out, his voice teasing yet layered with impatience. He was already halfway across the clearing, his hands shoved deep into the pockets of his worn jeans, a slight breeze tousling his dark hair. Ava could see the glint of mischief in his eyes, a spark that made her stomach flutter—both with annoyance and something deeper, something she feared to acknowledge.

“Just taking it in,” she replied, forcing a nonchalant tone as she stepped closer, the crunch of gravel beneath her boots punctuating her words. She focused on the ground, the way the pebbles shifted underfoot, a grounding sensation against the whirlwind of thoughts clamoring in her mind. This place—this moment—felt suspended in time, yet she knew that soon it would all rush back, the responsibilities and expectations closing in like a suffocating fog.

Liam turned, leaning back against a gnarled tree trunk, arms crossed. “You really think staring at the ground is going to change anything?” His smile was playful, but there was an undercurrent of seriousness that made her heart constrict.

“Maybe,” she said, her voice softer now, almost contemplative. “Maybe it helps to see where I’m stepping before I take the next leap.” She dared to meet his gaze, the intensity of his dark eyes holding hers like a tether.
